reviews.title: A nice approach to limiting screen time
reviews.text:
I've tried a lot of apps for limiting my screen time but most of them are structured on either what times I can block apps, or what amount of time I can go on those apps. These are really useful but this app works so well as an addition to them. In my case, I've set it up so that for every 15 minutes of language learning practice that I do, I get a reward of 15 minutes on Instagram. 

My favorite aspect is that now, after a recent update, my 15 minutes of Insta can now be measured in total usage instead of as a single block of time. Before, I only had the option to use up that 15 minutes in one go before the app was blocked again, which made me feel pressure to stay on my phone for the whole 15 minute or else sacrifice the reward I had just earned. Now if I get interrupted or just want to go do something else after checking a couple of messages on Insta, I can do so knowing that I can pick it back up again later for another 10 or so minutes if I want to.

reviews.title: Lovely reframe!
reviews.text:
I think this is a fantastic way to view a screen blocker. 

I love how easy it is to get started - I've been liking it a lot. I love the timers that count up quite a bit 

Constructive feedback for future releases: 

1. Make a way to delete habits that you built in the wrong style (I put crochet in manual checklist, but would be better in manual timer) 

2a. Is there any way to have it count the minutes your device is idle? Having the timer on means my screen is actively being used. I would love to "get credit" for not touching it or having it on me at all. 

2b. I don't have an Apple Watch so I have to carry my phone always to get step credit - it doesn't work with my Garmin. Related to 2a, I would love to be so engrossed in other stuff that I'm not even near my devices anymore

reviews.title: Good mission, but lots of bugs.
reviews.text:
The good: the 24 hour+ lock is great, good way to set up unbypasseable settings in a way that you can still technically reverse in a day if you figure out something is wrong. 
Location based is very clever and perfect for me since there are apps that I want to use when I’m out and about but are distracting when sitting at home. Only issue is it doesn’t work — location blocking only seems to update when you re-open the app, which defeats the purpose of it. 
After experimenting with location I decided I’d just add a time frame block like other apps do and call it a day until location is fixed. The only issue is that, with the most recent update it seems time frame has been removed. Perhaps I’m just missing it, but if not please add it back. 
Also: you should add a block for when Bluetooth is connected. Specifically when Bluetooth is in range, rather than just an unblock when Bluetooth is connected. I want to block certain apps when I’m at home, which means my car which is Bluetooth will be near me. But at work or when out with friends, I’ll be away from my car most of the time. And disabling Bluetooth should immediately force a block as you’re trying to get around it. 

Btw if location seems unfixable, I’d personally be happy with location + periodic block maybe every hour that only unblocks if you open the habits first app. That way, it’ll force a location refresh. You can have that as a lockable setting as a fallback. At least until you figure out a different fix. I want to support this app, I hope you fix these issues. Thanks n

reviews.text:

I first used it to restart my BrainHQ app training habit. I locked Youtube behind 5 minutes of BrainHQ, and suddenly I was using BrainHQ almost every day. 

When I saw I could unlock an ereader integration (KoReader) for a flat price and no subscription, I bought it. Now I read for an hour each morning on my ereader before I play my favorite phone game. 

Thank you for this app!

reviews.title: Why does the app function like it does
reviews.text:
Super cool concept a few things I don’t understand. 

When I complete a habit it gives me a timer for 10 min to use the app. Well I don’t necessarily know if I have 10min to use an app when I want to use it. I feel it should be a 10min time period allowed in the app that counts down whenever you use the app. Not just a timer for the app. So it counts off when I use the app not just 10 min where I use the app for 5 then close my phone for the next 5. 

Then I also am confused, I have many habits made but I can’t edit them once I create them. So if you mess something up or want to change how a habit works you have to create another habit then you have two similar habits to choose from. 


SO I make a block to block insta and YouTube. I then select 3 things to unlock whether I can watch it or not. Then I complete one of the habits and I still can’t watch YouTube till k complete the other two. So I figured I could create two blocks for both YouTube and insta and have two habits that can unlock and add 15 min to my allowed time. Well guess what, you have to unlock both blocks before being able to do any 15min. 

I dont know it doesn’t make sense to me because, I feel I should be able to do one habit and get 15 min then do another to have 2 unlocks banked for 30 min total. Not have to complete all blocks to unlock an app. Need some major fixes.

reviews.title: Finally an app I couldn’t find a way around
reviews.text:
I feel like I’ve tried every screen time app there is and I always ended up finding some way around it, which kind of defeats the whole purpose. I’ve done phone lock boxes, I’ve given my friends and family the passcode to my screen time so I couldn’t get to it, and I still found ways to bypass it. Honestly it got pretty bad and I kind of assumed nothing was going to work.

This app is different, I mean the developer must’ve been in the same spot as me because there are so many features that are exactly what I needed. The fact that I can’t delete it is insane to me. That was my first reaction to every other app, well none of this matters because I can just delete the thing that’s blocking me, and this one closes that off completely.

The part I think is actually the coolest is that the apps aren’t just gone. It’s not like the lock box where my whole phone is unusable, and it’s not like handing off a passcode where I have no access at all. I can still get into everything I block, I just have to do certain things first. That little difference of it actually being available but only after I do something I’ve realized is soooo helpful.

I’m going to email you because I have some ideas I think would make it even better, but it’s already so good. Really cool app, thank you!!

reviews.text:
Saw this app from Reysu, someone who I have loved watching since his first channel, and I have to say that this is a game changing app. His thoughts and principles have always been something I agreed with and seeing those implemented in the best screen-time app I’ve tried (and I’ve tried a lot) was amazing. 

All in all, it is an essential app to try if you’re trying to implement habits well. 

The only possible improvement (and this is frankly nitpicky) would be for apps that are blocked and only accessible after using an app for X number of minutes to be only be blocked in a specific timeframe so that I could use it whenever during the day but at night, when I can actually do the habit, it would then lock it until I used my reading app. Also, potentially making it so the bluetooth devices zone could block the apps and only be unblocked when out of their range, instead of vice versa like how it is currently. Great work though!!

reviews.title: Great concept, just needs a few improvements
reviews.text:
It seems like a really cool concept! Unfortunately, it doesn’t always block every app in the list. For example, I had messages selected, but it didn’t block it. It also didn’t block itself, even though I had Habits First in my list. It seems like it mostly works otherwise. 

The other thing keeping me from using it is that there just aren’t that many integrations that are useful to me personally. I think shortcuts should be included in the free version. I think that is essential. It seemed like it might be included but then it also says it’s only available in the pro version, so I don’t know. 

My final note is that the UI feels AI generated. I don’t know if it was for sure, but it’s definitely giving me AI vibes, even though many elements are native SwiftUI components.

Keep up the good work though! I think this is an awesome concept. It just needs a few improvements!
